transcript.text: If your dishwasher won't come on at all, the most common cause is simply that it isn't receiving electricity. This could be due to a tripped fuse, a loose plug, or a switched socket that has been turned off. Please check if the power cord is firmly plugged in and try plugging another device into the same socket to confirm it works. If the socket is live but the dishwasher still shows no signs of life (no lights or sounds), we need to look at the door latch mechanism, as a faulty safety switch will prevent the machine from starting.

other sockets and lights all work fine. its an integrated one so the plug isnt reachable, theres a switch above the worktop and its on with the little light lit. door is shut properly too. no lights or anything at all on the dishwasher

It sounds like the switch light indicates the circuit is live, but the dishwasher itself isn't receiving power. This often happens if the dedicated switched fused spur (a small box with a fuse inside, usually near the appliance) has tripped or blown, even if the wall switch looks on. Please check your fuse box for any specific fuses related to the kitchen or that appliance and see if one is off or needs resetting/replacing. If that fuse is fine, we'll need to look at the door wiring loom inside the dishwasher.
consumer unit has nothing tripped. i dont know how to check the fuse in the spur and ive no spare or meter. what now?

This points to a deeper internal issue like a broken door wiring loom or a failed control board. As an integrated appliance with no visible plug, you cannot safely access these components without removing the surrounding cabinetry and disconnecting the mains properly. This requires a qualified engineer to diagnose and fix. Please contact a professional repair service.

candidates: Power supply issue (trip, loose plug, or switched socket) (high)
Faulty door latch or safety switch (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "won't come on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Faulty door wiring loom or latch switch (medium)
